headline: 18 goals: Mbappe draws level with Messi in Golden Boot race
summary: Kylian Mbappe's brace against Sweden pushes him into a tie with Lionel Messi for the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot and second on the all-time scoring list.
details: Kylian Mbappe scored twice in France's 3-0 victory over Sweden in the Round of 32 at the New York-New Jersey Stadium, moving him level with Lionel Messi at the top of the Golden Boot race.
With these goals, Mbappe has now netted 18 goals in 18 appearances across three World Cups, surpassing German legend Miroslav Klose's 16 goals to take second place on the all-time scoring chart.
Only Lionel Messi remains ahead of the French forward, with 19 goals in 29 matches across six World Cup editions.
This marks the first time in history that two active players are simultaneously competing for both the Golden Boot and the World Cup's all-time scoring record.
France has now advanced to the last 16, where they will face Paraguay in Philadelphia this Sunday.
Paraguay secured their spot in the next round after stunning Germany in their Round of 32 match a day earlier.
caption:
18 goals in 18 games. Kylian Mbappe is now breathing down Lionel Messi's neck for the all-time World Cup scoring record!

Kylian Mbappe scored twice in France's 3-0 victory over Sweden in the Round of 32 at the New York-New Jersey Stadium, moving him level with Lionel Messi at the top of the Golden Boot race.

With these goals, Mbappe has now netted 18 goals in 18 appearances across three World Cups, surpassing German legend Miroslav Klose's 16 goals to take second place on the all-time scoring chart.

Only Lionel Messi remains ahead of the French forward, with 19 goals in 29 matches across six World Cup editions.

This marks the first time in history that two active players are simultaneously competing for both the Golden Boot and the World Cup's all-time scoring record.

France has now advanced to the last 16, where they will face Paraguay in Philadelphia this Sunday.

Paraguay secured their spot in the next round after stunning Germany in their Round of 32 match a day earlier.

headline_marked: Doha talks: [[Iran will not meet US envoys]] despite arrival in Qatar
headline: Doha talks: Iran will not meet US envoys despite arrival in Qatar
summary: High-level meetings are off the table as only technical talks on regional security will proceed, casting doubt on a lasting peace deal.
details: Top US envoys, including Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, have arrived in Doha, but a Qatari official confirmed they will not hold high-level meetings with Iranian representatives.
Instead, the focus will shift to technical discussions this week regarding regional security and other issues, which may be elevated to senior levels later.
The tension comes after exchanges of fire over the weekend that tested the interim accord signed between the US and Iran on June 17.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei stated that while dialogue with mediator Qatar regarding the release of frozen assets is likely, no meetings with the US are scheduled.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump described the potential Qatar meetings as "perhaps important, perhaps not," while Iran and Oman have reached a common understanding on the administration of the Strait of Hormuz.
In other regional developments, two members of Iran's Revolutionary Guards were shot dead in the city of Paveh, and Israeli drones attacked targets in southern Lebanon.
caption:
US envoys are in Doha, but Iran says no high-level meetings. Is the peace deal slipping away?

Top US envoys, including Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, have arrived in Doha, but a Qatari official confirmed they will not hold high-level meetings with Iranian representatives.

Instead, the focus will shift to technical discussions this week regarding regional security and other issues, which may be elevated to senior levels later.

The tension comes after exchanges of fire over the weekend that tested the interim accord signed between the US and Iran on June 17.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei stated that while dialogue with mediator Qatar regarding the release of frozen assets is likely, no meetings with the US are scheduled.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump described the potential Qatar meetings as "perhaps important, perhaps not," while Iran and Oman have reached a common understanding on the administration of the Strait of Hormuz.

In other regional developments, two members of Iran's Revolutionary Guards were shot dead in the city of Paveh, and Israeli drones attacked targets in southern Lebanon.
